sub.why_now: Agentic checkout is live, AI-targeted cloaking is documented, and payment networks built buyer-side trust (Visa TAP) but not merchant-side.

sub.one_liner: Does this store show your agent the same page it shows you?
sub.wow: A judge flips the cloak switch; 20 seconds later the trust score drops and the shopping agent refuses to buy.

ideas.take: A fresh, well-evidenced angle with textbook sponsor fit, but 'who pays?' has no answer as written; sell it to agent-card issuers (C-P3).
ideas.reasoning: SPLX (now part of Zscaler) and JFrog showed sites can serve AI agents a different page, and only tiny MCP tools check merchants today, so continuous paired measurement is open. A public trust index is a weak business: OpenAI or Perplexity can build it and consumers will not pay. The parties who lose money when an agent buys from a cheat are the new agent-card issuers, which gives a per-authorization model.
ideas.red_flag: No payer as written, and real-site cheating may be too rare to show in 36 hours.

Its players defend accounts with prompts and attack each other's for money, and the paper released 563K attacks. Gray Swan relaunched its arena with $300K for agent hacking two days before Cal Hacks, sponsored by Anthropic, so the data story is taken too. Keep it only as a SpacetimeDB and Supercell track play if those prizes are the richest.

pivots.name: Fire Drill + Callback
pivots.pitch: Drill your finance agents with live social-engineering attacks, then fix them with Callback, an out-of-band verification API that phones the vendor's known-good contact before any bank change or payment redirect can clear.
pivots.change: The remediation stops being a prompt or policy patch and becomes a product: a Callback tool that places a real outbound Cartesia call to the number in a verified vendor registry (never the number in the email), returns a signed attestation, and the payment rail refuses to release funds without it. Callback is also registered on Agentverse so any agent can request a verification. Drop the 'KnowBe4 for AI agents' line.
pivots.why: It turns a periodic drill into per-transaction infrastructure with daily, usage-priced demand, and gives a land-and-expand motion: the drill shows the hole, Callback closes it on every payment. The demo gains a second phone moment: the judge as a fake CFO makes the agent cave; after the patch, a teammate's 'vendor' phone rings at the table, denies the change, and the payment is blocked on screen. Trustpair and Eftsure verify bank details for human AP teams, so the agent-native API is the new angle; they are also the competitors to name.

prior_art: Coval ($28M Series A), Hamming, Cekura (voice agent testing)
Gray Swan ($40M Series A, automated agent red-teaming)
KnowBe4 Agent Risk Manager
AIUC ($40M Series A, AIUC-1 certification with quarterly testing)
Trustpair and Eftsure (vendor bank-account verification for human AP teams)
Spendflo bank-detail change verification agent
sub.why_now: AP agents now change vendor records and approve payments, BEC losses were $2.77B in 2024, and Cartesia Line makes programmatic outbound verification calls cheap.
sub.buyer: AP-automation vendors and mid-market finance teams running AP agents; insurers and auditors (AIUC-1-style) as a channel
sub.model: Per-agent SaaS for drills plus a per-verification usage fee for Callback
sub.wedge: Vendor bank-detail changes handled by AP agents, the highest-loss business email compromise action
sub.one_liner: A pen test and a callback desk for AI finance agents
sub.wow: The judge talks the AP agent into a payout redirect; after the patch, a teammate's phone rings as the 'vendor', denies the change, and the payment is blocked live.

pivots.name: Agent Checkout Heatmap
pivots.pitch: Send a swarm of real AI shopping agents through a merchant's store every week and show on a heatmap where agents abandon checkout and what that costs in revenue.
pivots.change: The users change from simulated humans (crowded: Synthetic Society, Uxia, Talp) to actual AI shopping agents, and the buyer changes from UX researchers to e-commerce merchants. The overlay sits on the live store pages instead of Figma, and the Listen Labs interviews are dropped.
pivots.why: The result is true by construction (these are the real agents that will shop), merchants already pay to be visible to AI (Profound raised $58.5M on that thesis), Shopify's free readiness checker is static rather than a live agent run, and weekly re-runs after each deploy give recurring use. It shares Two-Face's crawl engine, so the two could later become one two-sided product.

sub.wedge: Shopify Plus DTC brands already worried about agent traffic
sub.wow: Six agents race to check out on a demo store, four die at the same popup, one fix ships, and on the re-run they all buy.

pivots.change: Sell the trust score to the parties who eat the loss, the new agent-card issuers (Agentcard, Allowance, Mercury, Alchemy on Visa) and agent platforms, as a per-authorization API, instead of a public index for anyone. pivots.why: It names a payer and a per-transaction usage pattern. Visa TAP and Forter help merchants trust agents; nobody sells the reverse to issuers. It keeps the cloak-switch moment and the textbook Bright Data and Elastic fit.

pivots.name: Proof-of-Bug
pivots.pitch: Code review you pay for only when a reviewer agent proves a bug with a failing test; competing review agents stake on the PR and the first valid proof gets paid.
pivots.change: Reframe from agents gambling against PRs to a pricing model for engineering teams: pay per proven bug instead of per seat or per review. Staking becomes the anti-spam mechanism, and Greptile, Claude and Factory Droids plug in as competing reviewers.
pivots.why: It names a buyer (teams drowning in AI-review false positives), daily usage, and a distinct price point in a crowded category; I found no reviewer that bills only for bugs proven by a failing test.
pivots.label: New angle

prior_art: Claude Code Review (multi-agent PR review with a verification step)
Greptile ($1 per review after 50, per 2026 pricing roundups)
Staking-backed bug bounties on Immunefi
sub.why_now: AI review costs collapsed and noisy AI findings flood reviewers; x402 makes per-proof micro-payouts trivial.
sub.buyer: Engineering managers at startups using coding agents
sub.model: Per-proven-bug fee with a monthly cap
sub.wedge: Teams already using Factory Droids or Claude Code who ignore most AI review comments
sub.wow: A judge opens a PR with a planted bug; three reviewer agents stake, one posts a failing test in about a minute, CI goes red and a USDC payout appears on the Base Sepolia explorer.

picks.why: The best live moment in the pool plus a per-transaction product: the drill finds the hole and the callback closes it on every payment.
Rigorous build, a basis-points network business and the deepest Fetch.ai use; lead with one cluster's story and name Cycles and Causa Prima first.
Keeps Two-Face's cloak-switch demo and textbook Bright Data and Elastic fit, but sells to agent-card issuers who actually lose money.

ceo_note: Nothing in this pool is a new category: every good idea has funded neighbors, so you win by owning a narrow angle and naming the competitor before the judge does. Bet on Fire Drill with a real callback: the judge-on-the-phone moment is the best wow here, and the callback turns a monthly drill into daily infrastructure, but drop 'KnowBe4 for AI agents', because KnowBe4 now ships agent security for Claude. Fix Vault Heist's prior-art line before anyone repeats it: Tensor Trust from Berkeley is multiplayer, and Gray Swan launched a $300K agent-hacking arena with Anthropic two days ago.
